blocks.title: Hydrocarbons
blocks.text: Compounds containing carbon and hydrogen only in their molecules are called hydrocarbons.
On the basis of carbon skeleton, hydrocarbons are broadly classified into two types:

a) Hydrocarbons possessing open chain of carbon atoms are called open chain or acyclic hydrocarbons, or more commonly aliphatic hydrocarbons (aleiphatos is a Greek word meaning fat; fats have open chain structure). These can be further subdivided into saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) or unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes).

blocks.alt: A small yellow box: an oval labelled 'Aliphatic', a plus sign and an oval labelled 'Cyclic', joined by lines to a rectangle below labelled 'Alicyclic'.
blocks.caption: Aliphatic + cyclic: alicyclic (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.text: a) Hydrocarbons possessing rings of carbon atoms are called closed chain or cyclic hydrocarbons. These can be further divided into two types;

items: Some cyclic hydrocarbons both saturated and unsaturated which behave like aliphatic hydrocarbons, are called alicyclic hydrocarbons e.g, cycloalkanes, cycloalkenes etc.
Some cyclic hydrocarbons having benzene ring or resembling structures are called aromatic hydrocarbons, e.g., benzene, naphthalene, diphenyl methane etc.

blocks.alt: Two groups separated by a thick line. Aliphatic hydrocarbons: CH3-CH3 (ethane), H2C=CH2 (ethene), HC triple-bond CH (ethyne) and a hexagon (cyclohexane). Aromatic hydrocarbons, each ring drawn as a hexagon with a circle inside: benzene, methyl benzene (CH3 on the ring), naphthalene (two fused rings) and anthracene (three fused rings in a row).
